tip: Talvez triggers the subjunctive, so pedir becomes peça, not pede. The mood marks the outcome as uncertain.
Casual Brazilian commands use the he/she form: segura, not the textbook segure.
Negative commands switch to subjunctive endings: não jogue, not jogar. An a-verb like jogar takes -e.
Colloquial deixa eu plus an infinitive means let me: deixa eu terminar. Careful grammar would say deixe-me terminar.
Feelings take the subjunctive after que: fico feliz que você esteja, not está.
Tomar cuidado means be careful, literally take care: toma cuidado is the everyday warning.
Tomara que means let's hope and always takes the subjunctive: tomara que dê, from the verb dar.
For a future when, use the future subjunctive: quando chegar means when you arrive, not quando chega.
After a place word, mesmo means right or exactly: aqui mesmo means right here.
A gente means we or us in casual speech: pra gente means for us here.
The conditional would adds -ria endings to the whole infinitive: cozinhar plus íamos gives cozinharíamos.
A menos que means unless and always takes the subjunctive: a menos que você estude, not estuda.
Oxalá means hopefully, from Arabic, and forces the subjunctive: oxalá eu passe, not passo.
Puxar means to pull, not to push: puxa a porta. The push sign says empurre.
Precisar needs de before its object: precisariam de quantas cadeiras, how many chairs you would need.
Torcer literally means to wring, but torcer para is the verb for rooting for a team: torço para o Brasil.
Confiar pairs with em, and em plus ele contracts to nele: confio nele means I trust him.
Embora means although and always takes the subjunctive: embora ela seja jovem, not é jovem.
Valer a pena means to be worth the trouble: valha a pena reclamar means worth complaining.
Portuguese has haste rather than being in a hurry: ter pressa, so não precisa ter pressa means no need to rush.
Prestar atenção means to pay attention and takes em: presta atenção no is em plus o que.
Lembrar meaning to remember uses the reflexive with de: ele se lembre do aniversário.
Experimentar means to try or taste food, not to experiment: experimenta esse bolo means try this cake.
Respirar fundo means to breathe deeply, with fundo working as an adverb here, not fundamente.
When the person might not exist, the relative verb goes subjunctive: ninguém que fale, not fala.
Mesmo que means even if and takes the subjunctive: mesmo que você tente, not tenta.
Antes que means before and triggers the subjunctive: antes que eu esqueça, not esqueço.
